title: Totnes to Dartington Walk Route

images.title: River Dart at Totnes by Robin Drayton, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: River Dart at Totnes. The town is at the head of the estuary of the River Dart. Totnes has a long recorded history, dating back to 907, when its first castle was built. By the twelfth century it was already an important market town, and its former wealth and importance may be seen from the number of merchants' houses built in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Today, the town has a sizeable alternative and New Age community, known as a place where one can live a bohemian lifestyle

images.title: Dartington Hall by Chris Allen, CC BY-SA 2.0 <https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.0>, via Wikimedia Commons
images.caption: Dartington Hall. Dartington is home to an obsolete cider press (now the centrepiece of a shopping centre named after it), the Cott Inn, a public house dating from 1320, and Dartington Hall.

description: This walk takes you from Totnes to Dartington in Devon. The route links the two popular settlements, first following a riverside path along the River Dart before picking up a shared cycle and walking trail to take you to Dartington. On the way there are some lovely river and countryside views to enjoy. The route runs for a distance of 2 miles, passing along easy flat trails so is suitable for most abilities. In Dartington you can explore the lovely Dartington Hall Estate which includes hundreds of acres of parkland with beautiful gardens, riverside paths and peaceful woodland trails.
